title: Injury Incidence, Severity, and Type Across the Menstrual Cycle in Female Footballers: A Prospective Three Season Cohort Study
authors: Barlow A, Blodgett JM, Williams S, Pedlar CR, Bruinvels G
population: 26 elite professional female footballers over three seasons; 593 cycles over 13,390 days
findings: 74 injuries eligible; overall injury rate highest in the premenstrual phase (P4) vs menstruation (IIRR 2.30, 95% CI 0.99-5.34, P = 0.05).
P4 rates were higher for muscle injuries (IIRR 6.07, 95% CI 1.34-27.43, P = 0.02) and non-contact injuries (IIRR 3.05, 95% CI 1.10-8.50, P = 0.03).
Early luteal (P3) vs menstruation: muscle injuries IIRR 5.07 (95% CI 1.16-22.07, P = 0.03) and time-loss of 7 days or less IIRR 4.47 (1.01-19.68, P = 0.05).
Authors conclude injury risk was elevated in the luteal phase (P3 and P4) and call for urgent further research; no ACL injuries occurred.
limitations: 26 players, 74 injuries, very wide confidence intervals, football (contact, intermittent), elite athletes, no running data; single cohort not yet replicated.
implications: Add no cycle-phase injury multiplier to running load rules.
If cycle tracking is offered, show an optional awareness message (warm-up, hydration) for users who log a premenstrual phase; do not change prescribed load.
Optionally log injury onset with cycle day to build per-user data.
